messages:
alexa: Quick sync on continuous-batching scheduling decisions. We need a concrete path for how much caller info we accept and what the scheduler promises, especially for sustained long-run requests. My concern: if we let callers tell us sizes/deadlines freely, theyll game packing; if we hide everything the scheduler wastes bandwidth.

matt: TL;DR options?

alexa: Two axes: (A) queue topology: fixed lane-per-class vs single shared queue with dynamic shaping and reservations; (B) caller contract: blind enqueue (server infers shape) vs advisory shape hints vs explicit reservation.

ranjit: Experimented with advisory hints (clients send expected token_count + prefer_pack boolean). Using hints improved batch fill and reduced per-token p50 by ~10% on long requests. But it amplified head-of-line blocking for short interactive calls.

lucy: We should assume clients will try to optimize. That means any exposed hint must be treated as untrusted unless telemetry proves otherwise. Suggest a "trust score" per caller that gates how much weight we give to their hints.

matt: Agreed. Proposal: accept hints but mark them advisory. Admission API returns a ticket and an admission_decision object that includes used_shape and confidence. If confidence low, admission acts with server-estimated shape and increments a metric.

alexa: Example proto sketch:
```
Enqueue(Request) -> { ticket_id, admitted: true/false, used_shape: {tokens_est, bytes}, confidence: 0.0-1.0, retry_after_ms }
```
Rules: used_shape = client_hint if trust_score >= 0.75 && server_checks_pass else server-estimate.

sam: On preemption/eviction, runtime has hot KV state. If we evict without checkpointing KV slices, the regenerate cost hurts. We need a lightweight checkpoint protocol: scheduler sends PREEMPT_INTENT(ticket, grace_ms), runtime can respond with CHECKPOINT_READY and opaque handle. Scheduler can then move the ticket to a preserved queue with KV_handle. If runtime times out, scheduler force-evicts.

ranjit: For checkpoint format, keep it opaque: KV_handle is an id referencing a blob store entry. Runtime writes small KV deltas to a cache-backed blob, not full model state. That keeps latency low while enabling quick resume.

lucy: Add operational metrics: checkpoint_latency_ms, checkpoint_success_rate_by_model, resume_hit_rate. Also we need an alert on excessive force-evicts (indicates grace_ms too tight or heavy GC).

matt: Backpressure question: Do we apply token-bucket at ingress (early-reject) or accept + queue + later reject? Early-reject prevents wasted work (checkpoint attempts, KV thrash) and keeps tails bounded. But it's rough UX.

alexa: I favor early-reject for noisy tenants with clear retry semantics and retry-after. For mixed workloads we keep reserved capacity for small-latency buckets (e.g., < 64 tokens) so interactive traffic doesn't starve.

sam: Implementation detail: admission should check token-budget and per-tenant inflight_tokens. If inflight_tokens + requested_tokens > tenant_quota then return 429 with reason EXCEEDED_INFLIGHT and retry_after_ms.

ranjit: Simulation plan: run 50/50 short(8 token) vs long(1024 token) requests across 100 tenants, try three configs: lane-based with strict reservations, shared-queue w/ advisory hints + trust scoring, and shared-queue + no-client-hints. Measure p50/p95/p99 per-class, utilization, and checkpoint overhead.

lucy: Dashboard: panels for per-tenant tail latencies, queue depth histogram by size buckets, shape_hint_mismatch_rate, checkpoint_time_by_model, force_eviction_rate. Also add automated fallback mapping per route so we can degrade to smaller variants when latency trends up.

matt: Edge cases: malformed hints (clients lying), sudden large bursts (tenant spikes), runtime failing checkpoint (OOM), and cross-tenant starvation. We must document failure modes in RFC and specify fallbacks: demote hint -> server-estimate; if checkpoint fails -> force-evict + telemetry; if tenant spikes -> early-reject.

alexa: Decision proposal for RFC follow-up: 1) accept advisory shape_hints in API (advisory only), 2) implement per-caller trust_score to weight hints, 3) early-reject policy for inflight token budget with explicit retry-after, 4) soft-preempt checkpoint handshake that returns opaque KV_handle, 5) reserve small-latency slots for interactive requests.

ci-bot: ci: scheduler-protos v3 pushed, unit tests OK :white_check_mark: integration flaky on checkpoint tests :warning:

matt: I'll open the proto PR with admitted fields + used_shape/confidence by EOD.

ranjit: I'll run the sim matrix and post numbers by mid-week.

lucy: I'll sketch dashboards and alert rules, include sample queries for shape_hint_mismatch_rate.

sam: I'll draft the checkpoint handshake sequence diagram and list failure modes + mitigation.

alexa: Thanks all. If nobody objects I'll fold this into the RFC patch. tagging: @matt @ranjit @lucy @sam :thumbsup:

matt: +1

ranjit: +1

lucy: +1
